annotations.annotation_text: Page 500 opens Book 3, Chapter 3 ("The Inquest of Yawn") during the Age of Men phase. This passage continues the judicial inquest over the prostrate body of Yawn (Shaun), voices of the dead rising through him, HCE's final confession, featuring Yawn/Shaun, Mamalujo, HCE (voice), ALP (voice). The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.
sources: Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/annotationstofin0000mchu_h5g8

annotations.annotation_text: Issy/daughter figure "daughter" on page 500 ("The Inquest of Yawn"): the narcissistic mirror-daughter, modeled on Isolde and Swift's dual muses Stella and Vanessa, appears here within the judicial inquest over the prostrate body of Yawn (Shaun), voices of the dead rising through him, HCE's final confession. Her prismatic splitting into twenty-eight Rainbow Girls reflects the cycle's Age of Men phase through youthful seduction and self-reflection.
sources: Bédier, Joseph. The Romance of Tristan and Iseult. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/14244

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 500 ("The Inquest of Yawn"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Men dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind
